name: Temporal Lobe
summary: Handles hearing, language comprehension, memory formation, emotion, and face recognition. Contains the hippocampus and amygdala.

connections.note: Links memory and emotion with decision-making.
Connects Wernicke's area to Broca's area for language.

facts.text: The hippocampus is named after the Greek word for 'seahorse' due to its curved shape. It is one of only two brain regions where new neurons are born throughout adult life.
Patient H.M. had both hippocampi surgically removed to treat epilepsy. He could no longer form new long-term memories but retained memories from before the surgery.

detailedDescription: The temporal lobes sit behind the temples. The superior temporal gyrus houses the primary auditory cortex — where vibrations become conscious sound. Wernicke's area (left temporal lobe) handles language comprehension. Damage produces receptive aphasia — fluent but meaningless speech. The fusiform gyrus at the temporal-occipital boundary specializes in face recognition. Damage causes prosopagnosia — face blindness.
